newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Circus Circus cut to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Circus Circus cut to hold.

text.p: -- Salomon Bros analyst Bruce Turner said in a research note that he lowered his recommendation on Circus Circus to hold from buy.
-- "Our most significant concern with Circus Circus is largely beyond their control and is a function of the macro variables at work in Las Vegas," Turner said in the note.
-- The company reported fourth quarter earnings last week of $0.16 per share, $0.02 under Turner's forecast and below $0.35 netted one year ago.
-- Circus shares were off 5/8 at 30-7/8 in late morning New York Stock Exchange trade.
-- Turner also cut his Circus earnings estimates, to $1.50 from $1.80 for 1998 and to $1.65 from $2.20 for 1999.

-- ""Historically, the 'build it and they will come' rule has dominated the industry and new properties have stimulated excess demand. Yet 1996 appears to have shattered this pattern. Depsite seven percent Las Vegas-area room base expansion, 1996 baccarat-adjusted gaming revenue increased only 3.4 percent," Turner said.
-- "Of greater concern is data over the past six months showing a one percent decline in baccarat-adjusted gaming revenue," he said.

-- "The question to ponder: Have we reached the natural (demand) ceiling in Las Vegas? We believe it may be very close, yet investors should expect no alarm bells sounding the arrival of a demand ceiling. It will just gradually seep into valuations. As a result of our macro-related concerns, we expect lower returns on invested capital at older properties," he added.
